rows.speaker: خزاعة
rows.claim: One reported antecedent of “they” is Khuzāʿa, who said that the angels were God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: الضمير لخزاعة حيث قالوا : الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: Another reported antecedent is the Jews, who claimed God had intermarried with jinn and angels came from them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لليهود حيث قالوا : إنه سبحانه صاهر الجن فكانت منهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “took” suggests pretending or behaving as one who has a child.
rows.anchor: أي تكلف كما يتكلف من يكون له ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful is the one from whose beneficence every existent being derives.
rows.anchor: أي الذي كل موجود من فيض نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above having a child: that would imply a shared nature between Him and offspring, unlike the relation of beneficence to its true giver.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك يقتضي المجانسة بينه وبين الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are honored servants whom God created as He created others, not offspring, since servitude is incompatible with filial status.
rows.anchor: لا أولا د , فإن العبودية تنافي الولدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their honor consists in protection from error.
rows.anchor: مكرمون * } بالعصمة من الزلل , ولذلك فسر الإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not speak ahead of God’s permission; they say nothing He has not authorized and released them to say.
rows.anchor: لا يسبقونه } أي لا يسبقون إذنه { بالقول } أي بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They act only when He commands; their vigilance joins obedience in speech and action, the fullest form of obedience.
rows.anchor: فجمعوا في الطاعة بين القول والفعل وذلك غاية الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses the angels’ past, present, and future states; Biqāʿī offers two ways to assign what is before and behind them to known and unknown matters.
rows.anchor: أو يكون الأول لما عملوه والثاني لما لم يعلموه , لأنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels intercede in this life and the next only for those God approves, so people must not expect their intercession without His approval.
rows.anchor: ولا يشفعون } أي في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة { إلا لمن ارتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are continually apprehensive specifically from fear of God.
rows.anchor: وهم من خشيته } أي لا من غيرها { مشفقون * } أي دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī connects the communities’ division with the account of humanity once being one community and the People of the Book dividing after clear proof.
rows.anchor: ( { وما تفرق الذي أتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة } )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The effort of a believer who does righteous deeds is not nullified; God rewards it as deserved and adds from His bounty.
rows.anchor: بل نحن نجزيه عليه بما يستحقه ونزيده من فضلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God records the effort permanently; at judgment the person will be enabled to recall every deed, small or great, so none is lost.
rows.anchor: وما كتبناه فهو غير ضائع , بل باق , لنطلعه على يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the omitted cases of a disbeliever doing evil and a believer doing evil are left unmentioned to encourage faith.
rows.anchor: ولعله حذف هذين القسمين ترغيبا في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A destroyed community does not vanish under the earth without awareness: at death its people return to God and remain in the intermediate state, in lesser bliss or punishment before the greater one.
rows.anchor: بل إلينا بموتهم رجعوا فحبسناهم في البرزخ منعمين أو معذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening of the barrier described earlier is inevitable, and Gog and Magog then emerge among people.
rows.anchor: بفتح السد الذي تقدم وصفنا له , وأن فتحه لا بد منه

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir’s intensified reading suggests repeated openings or many people emerging from one opening; the other readers use the lighter form, compatible with one opening.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن عامر بالتشديد تدل على كثرة التفتيح أو على كثرة الخارجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadab means a raised rise of land; yansilūn means to hurry with quick, close steps like a wolf.
rows.anchor: من كل حدب } أي نشز عال من الأرض { ينسلون * } أي يسرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression may hint that the earth is spherical.
rows.anchor: وفي العبارة إيماء إلى أن الأرض كرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is the resurrection of the dead, which closely approaches and corresponds to what will actually occur.
rows.anchor: وهو حشر الأموات الذي يطابقه الواقع , إذا وجد قربا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form iftaʿala conveys an intensified nearness, likened to the Hour’s closeness when a pregnant woman is about to deliver.
rows.anchor: دلت صيغة ( افتعل ) على شدة القرب كما في الحديث أن الساعة إذ ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith is cited as comparing the Hour’s nearness at that time to a pregnant woman near term; no authority or grading is supplied here.
rows.anchor: كما في الحديث أن الساعة إذ ذاك مثل الحامل المتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden ifā may answer the conditional ifā directly and stand in place of fa; when fa also appears with it, the link between condition and result is reinforced.
rows.anchor: ويجوز وهو أقرب أن تكون إذا هذه الفجائية هي جواب إذا الشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ eyes are fixed and unblinking when the horrors they never expected appear before them.
rows.anchor: واقفة جامدة لا تطرف لما دهمهم من الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cry means that woe has arrived and become their companion, with no other helper or rescuer to call.
rows.anchor: حضرنا الويل فهو نديمنا فلا مدعو لنا غيره

words: قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say that in worldly life they were heedless of resurrection because they denied it.
rows.anchor: أي مبتدئة من اعتقاد هذا البعث فكنا نكذب به فعمتنا الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They correct their claim of heedlessness: the evidence was unmistakable, but they wronged themselves by refusing reflection, signs, and the messengers’ teaching.
rows.anchor: حيث أعرضنا عن تأمل دلائله , والنظر في مخايله , وتقبل كلام الرسل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening warning is placed alongside earlier passages on the Hour’s threat, divine punishment, reckoning, return, and the gathering of the dead.
rows.anchor: ( { ونضع موازين القسط يوم القيامة } )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links the earthquake’s timing to the scene of disbelievers’ fixed eyes after the barrier opens, which he takes to occur after people rise from their graves.
rows.anchor: فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا } ) 77 [ الأنبياء : 97 ] وما تبعه أن هذه الزلزلة بعد القيام من القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also relates the passage to the sky’s folding and the events of Sūrat al-Infiṭār, allowing these scenes to fall within the same long Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد هذا وا قبله لأن يوم الساعة طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “you see it” suits an earthquake witnessed by everyone, whereas “you see people” uses a singular observer because a person sees others as drunk, not himself.
rows.anchor: ولا يرى الإنسان السكر - إلا من غيره قال في الزلزلة { ترونها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People look intoxicated from bewilderment, shock, and amazement at the veil of divine might and majesty.
rows.anchor: لما هم فيه من الدهش والحيرة والبهت لما شاهدوا من حجاب العز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene denies that they are actually drunk from wine; the apparent drunkenness is caused by the severity and terror of God’s punishment, which overwhelms reason.
rows.anchor: ولكن عذاب الله } ذي العز والجبروت { شديد * } فهو الذي وجب

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِى ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction implies two groups: those who believe and fear the Day are saved, while others dispute God’s power and perish; the Day displays divine majesty, delighting God’s party and grieving Satan’s.
rows.anchor: فإن منكم من يؤمن فبتقي فينجو من شر ذلك اليوم الذي اقتضت الحكمة إظهار العظمة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputant challenges God’s power over the Day and His other affairs without knowledge, despite proof having come, and abandons sincere guides for falsehood.
rows.anchor: يجادل في الله } أي في قدرة الملك الأعظم على ذلك اليوم وفي غير ذلمك من شؤونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A marīd is wholly stripped for evil, has no other concern, and is intensely devoted to corruption.
rows.anchor: مريد * } أي متجرد للفساد لا شغل غيره , فهو في غاية الضراوة

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī says the word marīd derives from al-ʿurā.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي : وأصله العرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is decreed upon him” states the necessary consequence by naming what entails it, as a settled and unavoidable decree.
rows.anchor: كتب } أي قضى وقدر على سبيل الحتم الذي لا بد منه , تعبير باللازم عن الملزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To take the satan as patron is to treat him like an intimate ally by following him and accepting what he adorns.
rows.anchor: من تولاه } أي فعل معه فعل الولي مع وليه , باتباعه والإقبال على ما يزينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The satan makes obedience hateful and misleads his follower from the good path.
rows.anchor: بما يبغض إليه من الطاعات فيخطىء سبيل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the satan guides his follower anywhere, it is toward the Fire, by adorning desires that lead to sins.
rows.anchor: ويهديه } أي بما يزين له من الشهوات , الحاملة على الزلات , إعلاما بأنه إن كان له هدى إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address can include all people or be aimed specifically at deniers; “people” marks a low rank because deniers and those who act like them make up most people.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد المنكر فقط , وعبر بالناس الذي هو من أسفل الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional “if” rebukes the audience rather than expressing the author’s doubt; the past tense and “in” indicate that their misgiving is entrenched.
rows.anchor: وبين أنه ما عبر به إلا للتوبيخ , لا للشك في أمرهم , بجعل الشرط ماضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection means bodies rise with their souls as they were before death; God invokes creation to answer their considering this beyond His power.
rows.anchor: وهو قيام الأجسام بأرواحها كما كانت قبل مماتتها سواء , استعظاما لأن نقدر عليه

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī says the original sense of nuṭfa is a small amount of water.
rows.anchor: واصلها الماء القليل - قاله البغوي

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī derives nuṭfa from the idea of pouring.
rows.anchor: وأصل النطف الصب - قاله البيضاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿalaqa is a solid, red piece of blood without the capacity to flow.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة دم حمراء جامدة , ليس فيها أهلية للسيلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍgha is a very small piece of flesh into which the sperm develops.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة لحم صغيرة جدا تطورت إليها النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some embryos are brought to complete human form; others are not completed, miscarry, are corrupted by heat, or form only incompletely despite having a spirit.
rows.anchor: وتارة لا يخلقها بل يخرجها من الرحم فاسدة , أو تحرقها حرارته , أو غير مخلقة تخليقا تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī gives Shaqq, described as half a human, and Satiḥ, described as an upper body without a lower one, as examples of incomplete formation.
rows.anchor: كشق الذي كان شق آدمي , وسطيح الذي كان علوا بلا سفل ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The developmental variations display God’s complete power and wisdom; variation disproves nature as the cause, since nature would not produce differing outcomes.
rows.anchor: كمال قدرتنا , وتمام حكمتنا , وأن ذلك ليس كائنا عن الطبيعة , لأنه لو كان عنها لم يختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “make clear” is omitted to encompass anything human understanding can grasp.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول إشارة إلى أنه يدخل فيه كل مل يمكن أن يحيط به العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves in the womb and completes whichever embryo He chooses.
rows.anchor: أي من ذلك الذي خلقناه { ما نشاء } إتمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term may be six months or longer, according to the strength of the womb and fetus, their nourishment, and other conditions known only to their creator.
rows.anchor: قدرناه لإتمامه ما بين ستة أشهر إلى ما نريد من الزيادة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God does not choose to complete is expelled before completion or consumed by the womb’s heat and disappears.
rows.anchor: فإن الأرحام تمجه بقدرتنا وتلقيه دون التمام أو تحرقه فيضمحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infants emerge small and weak in body and senses, so their size does not destroy their mothers at birth.
rows.anchor: من صغر الجثة وضعف البدن والسمع والبصر وجميع الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages run from nursing through youth, puberty, and full strength; each person reaches the limit of strength appointed for them.
rows.anchor: فيما بين الرضاع , إلى حال اليفاع , إلى زمان الاحتلام , وقوة الشباب والتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die before reaching old age, while others are returned to it and lose their powers.
rows.anchor: ومنكم من يتوفى } قبل ما بعد ذلك من سن الشيخوخة { ومنكم من يرد } بالشيخوخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form portrays the return to old age as easy for God, though it would seem unlikely without repeated observation.
rows.anchor: وبناه للمجهول إشارة إلى سهولته عليه مع استبعاده لولا تكرر المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most decrepit age is senescence, when all one’s powers decline.
rows.anchor: وهو سن الهرم فينقص جميع قواه

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive min marks the short interval between knowledge and its loss; omitting a stated endpoint allows that knowledge may return or ignorance may last until death.
rows.anchor: أثبت ( من ) الابتدائية للدلالة على قرب زمن الجهل من زمن العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī contrasts the omitted endpoint here with the wording previously discussed in Sūrat al-Naḥl, which does not allow the same implication of possible recovery.
rows.anchor: وأفهم غسقاط حرف الانتهاء أنه ربما عاد إليه علمه , وربما اتصل جهله بالموت بخلاف ما مضى في النحل

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s sudden loss of learning and return to childlike weakness show a voluntary divine act; nature would cause continued growth, and the one who reverses life can restore the dead.
rows.anchor: وقد علم - بعود الإنسان في ذهاب العلم وصغر الجسم إلى نحو ما كان عليه في ابتداء الخلق - قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the argument from human development, Biqāʿī adds a visible proof from the earth as the passage moves from an unseen first creation to sensible evidence.
rows.anchor: وكان أول الإيجاد فيه غير مشاهد فعبر عنه بما يليق به , أتبعه دليلا آخر محسوسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “you see” addresses each suitable observer individually.
rows.anchor: ولعله أفرد الضمير توجيها إلى كل من يصلح أن يخاطب بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is dry, level, and still like a corpse, with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي يابسة مطمئنة ساكنة سكون الميت ليس بها شيء من نبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain comes by God’s mighty power from a place where it is not otherwise found.
rows.anchor: فننزل عليها ماء من مكان لا يوجد فيه ثم ينزل منه بقدرة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth quivers as plants sprout and comes alive, ready to produce vegetation; al-Rāzī defines the motion as vigorous movement in different directions.
rows.anchor: والاهتزاز : شدة الحركوة في الجهات المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It swells, its first visible sign, and grows through the vegetation formed from soil and water.
rows.anchor: أي انتفخت , وذلك أول ما يظهر منها للعين وزادت ونمت بما يخرج منهاا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “pair” here means a plant kind matched with another kind that completes its usefulness.
rows.anchor: أي صنف عادلناه بصنف آخر جعلناه تمام نفعه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vegetation delights the senses through its varied colors, tastes, scents, forms, uses, and sizes.
rows.anchor: في اختلاف ألوانها وطعومها , وورائحها وأشكالها , ومنافعها ومقاديرها

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī compares plants’ movement from deficiency to perfection with humans’ progress toward their perfected state in resurrection: eternal life, sufficiency, knowledge, purity, and freedom from worldly defects for the blessed.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : فكما أن النبات يتوجه من نقص إلى كمال , فكذلك الآدمي يترقى من نقص إلى كمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the preceding sūra as establishing God’s omnipotence and will, and its conclusion as affirming His knowledge; the present verse answers the implied question about His rule over countless creatures and their states.
rows.anchor: ولما كان جميع ما تقدم في هذه السورة دالا على أنه على كل شيء قدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd here means submission to God, being governed by His command and subjected to His will like a devoted worshipper.
rows.anchor: أي يخضع منقادا لأمره مسخرا لما يريد منه تسخير من هو في غاية الاجتهاد

words: مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun reinforces universal sovereignty; if the phrase includes nonrational beings by predominance, their submission follows a fortiori, and if it means rational beings, nonrational submission follows all the more.
rows.anchor: أكد بإعادة الموصول فقال : { ومن في الأرض } إن أخلت غير العاقل فبالتغليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies are singled out as objects worshipped instead of God by various tribes.
rows.anchor: لأن كلا منهما عبد من دون الله أو عبد شيء منه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān assigns sun worship to Himyar, moon to Kināna, Aldebaran to Tamīm, Sirius to Lakhm, the Pleiades to Ṭayyiʾ, Mercury to Asad, and al-Mirzam to Rabīʿa.
rows.anchor: فعبد الشمس حمير , والقمر كنانة , والدبران تميم , والشعرى لخم , والثريا طيىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains supply material for idols, some trees are worshipped, and cattle are among the animals worshipped; all such beings submit to God’s command.
rows.anchor: الجبال } أي التي تنحت منها الأصنام { والشجر } التي عبد بعضها { والدواب } التي عبد منها البقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these creatures are nonrational, God’s command to them is what He wills them to do.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم لكون هذه لا تعقل - أن أمره لها هو مراده منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are already included among those on earth, but are singled out because their praiseworthy prostration is obedient worship that earns reward, not mere compliance with divine will.
rows.anchor: وكان السجود الممدوحون عليه إنما هو الموافق للأمر , لا الموافق للإرادة المجردة عن الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject the binding command after proof is established deserve punishment; they may still “prostrate” in the lexical sense of conforming to God’s will while being unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فجحد الأمر الذي من جحده كان كافرا وإن كان كافرا وإن كان ساجدا عابدا بالمعنى اللغوي الذي هو

words: وَكَثِيرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: affirming prostration for the first group implies its absence in the second, while mentioning punishment for the second implies reward for the first.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : إثبات السجود في الأول دليل على انتفائه في الثاني , وذكر العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On an analysis that supplies a repeated governing word with a different sense, the construction approaches istiḫdām, where a pronoun follows a word intended in another sense.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول بأن هذا في تقدير عامل من لفظ الأول بغير معناه هو قريب من الاستخدام

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God honors with the ability to obey cannot be humiliated, and whoever He humiliates by rejecting His command has no one able to honor them; humiliation is emphasized in keeping with the threat and display of power.
rows.anchor: من يهن الله } أي الذي له الأمر كله بمنابذة أمره { فما له من مكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If any other agent could oppose God even momentarily, He would not do whatever He wills; hence no one acts independently of Him.
rows.anchor: فلو جاز أن يمانعه غيره ولو في لحظة لم يكن فاعلا لما يشاء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr quotes Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s report of ʿAlī questioning a man about divine will: the man admits God wills his creation, illness, healing, and destination; ʿAlī threatens him if he answered otherwise. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير : قال ابن أبي حاتم : حدثنا أحمد بن شيبان الرملي نا القداح عن جعفر بن محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading of “permission was given” presents the granting of permission as easy for God.
rows.anchor: وأشار بقراءة من بنها للمجهول إلى سهولة ذلك عليه سبخانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those capable of defense are now permitted to fight after being prevented in Mecca and instructed to pardon.
rows.anchor: للذين يقاتلون } أي للذين فيهم قوة المدافعة , في المدافعة بالقتلا بعد أن كانوا يمنعون منه بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason for permission is that the oppressors expelled and harmed the believers without right.
rows.anchor: بأنهم ظلموا } أي وقع ظلم الظالمين لهم بالإخراج من الديار , والأذى بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī allows “God is able to help them” to coordinate with the earlier statement that God repels people, making permission part of that divine defense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عطفه على قوله { إن الله يدفع } أي بإذنه لهم في القتال وأنه { على نصرهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording answers how unlikely victory seemed when the opponents were many and strong and the believers few and weak.
rows.anchor: وأبلغ في التأكيد لا ستبعاد النصرة إذ ذاك بالكفار من الكثرة والقوة , وللمؤمنين من الضعف والقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expelled believers were driven to the mountain valley, Abyssinia, and Medina.
rows.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم } إلى الشعب والحبشة والمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their only alleged offense was professing God as Lord, a statement that should instead have secured their residence, love, praise, and emulation.
rows.anchor: الموجب لإقرارهم في ديارهم , وحبهم ومدحهم واقتفاء آثارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be parsed as disconnected, meaning they had no offense apart from their confession, or as an ordinary exception; either way it frames their confession as the sole pretext for expulsion.
rows.anchor: فهو من باب : ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic example feigns criticism of swords blunted in battle while actually praising their owners’ valor.
rows.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who are sincerely devoted to God attract people’s arrows of intrigue and every effort to harm them.
rows.anchor: من أخلص لله , صوب الناس إليه سهام مكرهم , ولم يدعوا في أذاه شيئا من جهدهم

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repelling people through others operates in every religious law and in the era of every prophet; the permission for these believers illustrates that wider principle.
rows.anchor: في كل شريعة , وفي زمن كل ني أرسله

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without this repulsion, polytheism would remain openly dominant and ignorant people would seize the pilgrimage sites.
rows.anchor: لا ستمر الشرك ظاهرا , والباطل - باستيلاء الجهلة على مواطن الحج - قاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list names elevated small retreats of monks, Christian churches, Jewish synagogues, and Muslim mosques, respectively.
rows.anchor: صوامع } وهي معابد صغار مرتفعة للرهبان { وبيع } للنصارى { وصلوات } اي كنائس اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques come last in the list so that they are farthest from demolition and nearest in the wording to mention of God’s name.
rows.anchor: أخرها لتكون بعيدة من الهدم قريبة من الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using God’s name explicitly instead of a pronoun may signal that the groups invoke Him differently in these places, with varying degrees of sincerity.
rows.anchor: ولعل العدول عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار للإشارة إلى اختلاف ذكره تعالى في الأماكن المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God averts destruction because each religious group may seek to ruin another group’s sanctuaries, and even members of one faith may attack one another’s places of worship.
rows.anchor: لأن كل فرقة تريد هدم ما للأخرى , بل ربما أراد بعض أهل ملة إخراب بعض معلبد أهل ملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God counters the corruption He wills among most people by placing opposing forces among them, which reduces much of their stubbornness.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى لما أراد بأكثر الناس الفساد , نصب لهم من الأضداد , ما يخفف كثيرا من العناد
